Siam Cement PCL/The’s 2021 Insolvency: Reflecting on a Major Disruption in Thailand’s Construction Sector

Three years after the 2021 insolvency of Siam Cement PCL/The, the shockwaves that once rattled the construction materials industry in Thailand have faded, allowing the sector to stabilize. At the time, the company’s entry into court-administered restructuring marked the largest such case in the nation’s building materials history, affecting both its operations and confidence in the broader sector.

Siam Cement PCL/The, long considered a cornerstone of Thailand’s construction supply chain, was forced into insolvency following a sharp downturn in the property market and rising debt burdens aggravated by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2021, the company announced it would halt several manufacturing lines and suspend shipments from its flagship Saraburi plant. Layoffs affecting more than 2,000 employees soon followed.

“Everyone in the industry felt the impact immediately,” recalled Suriya Tangsiri, president of the Thai Construction Materials Association. “Projects were delayed across the country as contractors scrambled to find alternative suppliers for cement and related products.”

The National Labour Union reported that the sudden closure of plants led to a surge in unemployment claims in central regions, but noted that most affected workers found new positions within a year as smaller competitors expanded to fill the gap.

By late 2022, the company’s assets were liquidated, with key facilities acquired by new entrants such as Eastern Concrete Group Ltd. Analysts say the restructuring paved the way for increased competition and diversification in the market.

“There was a period of uncertainty, but the market has since normalized,” said Chanin Phongchai, an industry analyst at BaanSuan Research. “Supply chains have adjusted, and there is no current disruption to construction projects.”

Today, the effects of Siam Cement PCL/The’s insolvency are viewed as a turning point that forced the industry to adapt and modernize, with stakeholders emphasizing the importance of resilience and risk management.
